newsitem.title: USA: Three glasses of milk a day keeps doctor away.
newsitem.headline: Three glasses of milk a day keeps doctor away.

text.p: Three glasses of milk a day is the goal of a new public health campaign launched Wednesday to correct widespread calcium defiencies in the American diet.

The new "Drink 3" campaign, a joint venture of health groups and the milk industry, will debut on the sides of milk cartons and on the Internet and reinforce TV and billboard advertisments showing celebrities wearing milk moustaches.
Adults need 1,000 mg of calcium a day, about the amount found in three glasses. But only 1 in 10 women and one-third of men get that amount of calcium.
Low calcium intake is one of the three most significant nutritient deficiencies, according to public health officials' Healthy People 2000 programme.

"Unfortunately the gap between recommended and actual calcium intake is quite wide and we haven't seen any improvement in recent years," said Sandra Raymond, executive director of the National Osteoporosis Foundation.

Milk contains calcium, which is needed for strong bones and to protect against the brittle bones of osteoporosis later in life. But it also contains other vitamins and minerals nutrients that are throught to protect the heart and the cardiovascular system.
Many people are reluctant to drink whole milk because of its fat content but nonfat or 1 percent fat milk have the nutrients without the fat.
